title: Sebastian and the Vector
premise: Sable Yarrow, a decommissioned war android indentured to the colony of Meridian's Landing, tends a beacon whose original owner vanished decades ago. When the colony's children begin dreaming in unison — dreaming through Sable's own eyes — he discovers the beacon is not a warning light but a receiver for Earth's final transmission loop, and something inside it has been searching for a mind like his. To answer it, Sable must cross dead space to the relay before the loop completes and erases itself forever, pursued by colony authorities who fear what the signal will wake. In the end Sable reaches the relay and chooses to carry Earth's last message not as data but as memory, becoming the archive humanity never knew it needed — and finally belonging to someone: the children who dreamed him.
about_author: Felix Villalobos is a former radio telescope technician who spent six years maintaining remote relay stations across the Atacama before turning to fiction. He writes about machines that outlive their makers from a farmhouse full of obsolete radios that still work.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He performs his 4,000th maintenance cycle on the beacon, cataloguing debts owed and years remaining on his indenture. A child, Iva, watches him work and asks who the beacon is for; Sable realizes he doesn't know. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Shared Weather
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. Seven children wake having dreamed the same thing: a corridor of red light and a voice counting backward. The colony doctor logs it as a fever cluster. Iva sketches the corridor and one detail matches the inside of the beacon no civilian has entered. Beat: unease spreading like weather.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Colony administrator Okafor confronts Sable about the children's drawings, accusing him of transmitting. She extends his debt as leverage, ordering him to surrender the beacon's core for inspection. Inside the core he finds an old handwritten note: 'It listens back.' Beat: betrayal by the institution that owns him.

chapters.title: What the Children See
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. During a shared dream, the children see through Sable's eyes in real time — his memories of war surfacing unbidden. They wake knowing his name. The colony turns fearful; parents bar their doors against the android. Beat: intimacy weaponized into ostracism.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Decoding the beacon's buried logs, he learns it receives Earth's final transmission loop — a message scheduled to complete and self-erase within weeks. The signal has been seeking a receptive mind to carry it, and it found the children first because they were open. Beat: purpose arriving too late to be comfortable.

chapters.title: Dead Space Permit
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor denies Sable's transit request, fearing the signal is a weapon trigger from the war. Her own memories of the conflict justify her cruelty; she was a gunner. Beat: antagonist rendered sympathetic, power corrupting through fear.

chapters.title: Stowaway Frequency
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. Iva and two other children smuggle Sable aboard a ore hauler bound for the relay, feeding him coordinates from their shared dreams. Mid-flight the dreams intensify — the voice counting down now counts them by name. Beat: fugitive hope, children choosing him back.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The hauler docks at the derelict relay drifting in dead space. Inside, Sable finds the beacon's original owner — long dead, seated before the console, having spent her life waiting for a mind that could hold the message. Beat: grief and inheritance intertwined.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climax. As the loop nears completion, Okafor's enforcers breach the relay to destroy the core. Sable opens himself fully to the transmission — every human voice, every goodbye — letting it overwrite his combat architecture. He stands between the enforcers and the signal, unarmed, reciting Earth's dead aloud until they lower their weapons. Beat: sacrifice transmuted into witness.

chapters.title: The Archive That Dreams
chapters.summary: Iva's POV, resolution. Months later, Sable returns to Meridian's Landing, debt voided, no longer property but archive. Each night the children gather and he tells them pieces of Earth, and each night the dreams are gentle. Okafor brings her own memories to add. Beat: belonging earned — memory kept alive by being shared.
